title: SQL Server Complete Cheat Sheet
description: Comprehensive quick reference for SQL Server: SELECT, JOINs, CTEs, window functions, indexes, transactions, stored procedures, and performance tuning.

data.text: SQL Server is a relational database management system by Microsoft. Use T-SQL for querying and managing data.

data.title: SELECT Basics
WHERE Clause
ORDER BY
INNER JOIN
data.code:
-- Basic inner join
SELECT Orders.Id, Customers.Name
FROM Orders
INNER JOIN Customers ON Orders.CustomerId = Customers.Id;

-- Joining 3+ tables
SELECT Orders.Id, Customers.Name, Products.Name AS ProductName
FROM Orders
INNER JOIN Customers ON Orders.CustomerId = Customers.Id
INNER JOIN OrderItems ON Orders.Id = OrderItems.OrderId
INNER JOIN Products ON OrderItems.ProductId = Products.Id;

data.title: LEFT JOIN
data.content: Include all rows from left table.
data.code:
-- All customers with their orders
SELECT Customers.Name, Orders.Id AS OrderId
FROM Customers
LEFT JOIN Orders ON Customers.Id = Orders.CustomerId;

-- LEFT JOIN with NULL handling
SELECT Customers.Name, ISNULL(COUNT(Orders.Id), 0) AS OrderCount
FROM Customers
LEFT JOIN Orders ON Customers.Id = Orders.CustomerId
GROUP BY Customers.Name;

data.title: RIGHT & FULL JOIN
data.code:
-- RIGHT JOIN - all rows from right table
SELECT Customers.Name, Orders.Id
FROM Orders
RIGHT JOIN Customers ON Orders.CustomerId = Customers.Id;

-- FULL OUTER JOIN - all rows from both
SELECT Customers.Name, Orders.Id
FROM Customers
FULL OUTER JOIN Orders ON Customers.Id = Orders.CustomerId;

data.title: CROSS & SELF JOIN
data.code:
-- CROSS JOIN (Cartesian product)
SELECT Sizes.Name, Colors.Name
FROM Sizes
CROSS JOIN Colors;

-- SELF JOIN (employee-manager)
SELECT E.Name AS Employee, M.Name AS Manager
FROM Employees E
LEFT JOIN Employees M ON E.ManagerId = M.Id;

-- CROSS APPLY
SELECT C.Name, O.Total
FROM Customers C
CROSS APPLY (
  SELECT SUM(Amount) AS Total FROM Orders WHERE CustomerId = C.Id
) O;

data.title: Aggregates
data.code:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS TotalOrders,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerId) AS UniqueCustomers,
  SUM(Amount) AS TotalRevenue,
  AVG(Amount) AS AvgOrder,
  MIN(Amount) AS MinOrder,
  MAX(Amount) AS MaxOrder
FROM Orders;

data.title: GROUP BY & HAVING
data.code:
-- Group by single column
SELECT CustomerId, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerId;

-- HAVING (filter after grouping)
SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Amount) AS Total
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerId
HAVING SUM(Amount) > 1000;

-- ROLLUP
SELECT Category, SUM(Amount) AS Total
FROM Orders
GROUP BY ROLLUP(Category);

data.title: Subquery Patterns
Common Table Expressions
data.code:
-- Basic CTE
WITH CustomerOrders AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount, SUM(Amount) AS Total
  FROM Orders
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT C.Name, CO.OrderCount, CO.Total
FROM Customers C
INNER JOIN CustomerOrders CO ON C.Id = CO.CustomerId;

-- Recursive CTE (employee hierarchy)
WITH OrgChart AS (
  SELECT Id, Name, ManagerId, 1 AS Level
  FROM Employees WHERE ManagerId IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT E.Id, E.Name, E.ManagerId, OC.Level + 1
  FROM Employees E
  INNER JOIN OrgChart OC ON E.ManagerId = OC.Id
)
SELECT * FROM OrgChart;

data.title: Window Functions
data.code:
-- ROW_NUMBER
SELECT Name, Salary,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS RowNum
FROM Employees;

-- RANK vs DENSE_RANK
SELECT Name, Salary,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS Rank,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY Salary DESC) AS DenseRank
FROM Employees;

-- Running total
SELECT Date, Amount,
  SUM(Amount) OVER (ORDER BY Date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS RunningTotal
FROM Sales;

data.title: PIVOT
String Manipulation
data.code:
SELECT
  CONCAT('Hello', ' ', 'World') AS Greeting,
  CONCAT_WS(', ', 'A', 'B', 'C') AS CommaList,
  UPPER('hello') AS Upper,
  LOWER('HELLO') AS Lower,
  LTRIM('  text') AS TrimmedLeft,
  RTRIM('text  ') AS TrimmedRight,
  LEN('hello') AS Length,
  SUBSTRING('hello', 1, 3) AS Sub,
  REPLACE('hello world', 'world', 'SQL') AS Replaced,
  CHARINDEX('l', 'hello') AS Position,
  FORMAT(GETDATE(), 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS Formatted;

data.title: Date Operations
data.content: Working with dates in SQL Server.
data.code:
SELECT
  GETDATE() AS Now,
  DATEADD(day, 7, GETDATE()) AS NextWeek,
  DATEDIFF(day, '2024-01-01', GETDATE()) AS DaysDiff,
  DATENAME(month, GETDATE()) AS MonthName,
  DATEPART(year, GETDATE()) AS Year,
  EOMONTH(GETDATE()) AS EndOfMonth,
  CONVERT(date, GETDATE()) AS DateOnly,
  CAST(GETDATE() AS date) AS DateOnly2;

data.title: CASE Expressions
data.code:
-- Simple CASE
SELECT Name,
  CASE Status
    WHEN 1 THEN 'Active'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'Pending'
    ELSE 'Inactive'
  END AS StatusText
FROM Users;

-- Searched CASE
SELECT Name,
  CASE
    WHEN Age < 18 THEN 'Minor'
    WHEN Age < 65 THEN 'Adult'
    ELSE 'Senior'
  END AS AgeGroup
FROM Users;

-- COALESCE & ISNULL
SELECT COALESCE(Phone, Email, 'N/A') AS Contact;
SELECT ISNULL(Phone, 'N/A') AS Phone;

data.title: Creating Indexes
Table Constraints
data.code:
CREATE TABLE Orders (
  Id INT PRIMARY KEY IDENTITY(1,1),
  CustomerId INT NOT NULL,
  Amount DECIMAL(10,2) CHECK (Amount > 0),
  Status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Pending',
  CreatedAt DATETIME DEFAULT GETDATE(),
  CONSTRAINT FK_Orders_Customers FOREIGN KEY (CustomerId)
    REFERENCES Customers(Id)
    ON DELETE CASCADE
);

MERGE
data.content: Insert, update, or delete based on match.
data.code:
MERGE INTO TargetTable AS T
USING SourceTable AS S
ON T.Id = S.Id
WHEN MATCHED THEN
  UPDATE SET T.Name = S.Name, T.Amount = S.Amount
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN
  INSERT (Id, Name, Amount) VALUES (S.Id, S.Name, S.Amount)
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN
  DELETE;

Multiple CTEs
data.code:
WITH TopCustomers AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Amount) AS TotalSpent
  FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerId
),
HighValueOrders AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, COUNT(*) AS HighValueCount
  FROM Orders WHERE Amount > 500 GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT C.Name, TC.TotalSpent, HV.HighValueCount
FROM Customers C
INNER JOIN TopCustomers TC ON C.Id = TC.CustomerId
INNER JOIN HighValueOrders HV ON C.Id = HV.CustomerId
WHERE TC.TotalSpent > 1000
ORDER BY TC.TotalSpent DESC;

data.title: NULL Handling
data.code:
-- NULLIF: returns NULL if two values are equal
SELECT NULLIF(5, 5);   -- NULL
SELECT NULLIF(5, 3);   -- 5

-- COALESCE: returns first non-NULL value
SELECT COALESCE(NULL, NULL, 'default', 'other') AS Result; -- 'default'

-- Practical: avoid division by zero
SELECT Amount / NULLIF(Quantity, 0) AS UnitPrice
FROM OrderItems;

data.title: NULL Comparison
data.code:
-- ISNULL: SQL Server specific, uses first value type
SELECT ISNULL(NULL, 0) AS Result;       -- 0 (int)
SELECT ISNULL(NULL, 'default') AS Result; -- 'default' (varchar)

-- COALESCE: ANSI SQL standard, returns highest precedence type
SELECT COALESCE(NULL, 0, 'default') AS Result; -- 0 (int)

-- Performance: ISNULL is usually faster
-- Use ISNULL for simple replacements, COALESCE for ANSI compliance
